svg.aria-label: POC flow: a data engineer asks Claude Code which pipelines failed; Claude calls list_failed_runs through the MCP client and server.py, which queries PostgreSQL; then it calls get_run_details for each run and explains the failures.
svg.text: Our POC: “Which pipelines failed on 2026-11-15, and why?”
On-call triage in plain English, without giving the AI database credentials or free-form SQL
1 · You ask Claude Code: “Which pipelines failed on 2026-11-15, and why?”
2 · Claude picks list_failed_runs from the tools it discovered
3 · The MCP client sends a JSON-RPC tools/call to the MCP server over stdio
4 · The repository runs a parameterized SELECT in a READ ONLY transaction
5 · PostgreSQL returns 2 FAILED runs; they come back to Claude as a tool result
6 · No cause yet, so Claude decides on its own to call get_run_details for each run
7 · Full audit records (source, target, error_message) return to Claude
8 · Claude explains: lost Spark executor (202) and schema mismatch on amount (203)
On the wire: real JSON-RPC from this POC
What Claude answered (real Claude Code run)
likely a lost executor; a plain re-run usually works
• 203 payments_ingest: amount arrived as STRING, not DECIMAL
data-contract break; fix upstream or cast before load
• only 2 read-only tools, no arbitrary SQL
• parameterized queries in a READ ONLY transaction
• connection settings from environment, never in code
• the LLM never sees the database credentials
